newsitem.title: UK: Intl CableTel bids for UK TV licences.
newsitem.headline: Intl CableTel bids for UK TV licences.

text.p: International CableTel said on Friday that it had submitted a bid to run three digital terrestrial television multiplexes in the UK.
U.S.-owned cable company International CableTel is the third largest cable operator in the UK and owns NTL, one of two major British transmission companies.
The bid has been submitted in the name of a new company called Digital Television Network, wholly owned by International CableTel.
DTN chief executive Jeremy Thorp said newspaper reports linking the group to United News & Media Plc, French television subscription company Canal Plus and merchant bank Merrill Lynch were unfounded.
"We think we have the perfect team," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview. "Obviously there will be substantial start-up costs," he added.
A rival venture between BSkyB, Granada Group and Carlton Communications has said that initial funding may be as high as 300 million stg. Thorp said it would be in that region.

DTN said it had made arrangements with several major consumer electronics manufacturers to produce digital terrestrial television (DTT) set-top boxes which will be compatible with satellite and cable services.
DTN said it would be supported by world-class programmes from ITN and leading Hollywood studios.
